overall_reason: The 'backbone of global commerce' tiles give each figure a worded qualifier and period ('US$1.9tn in payments volume processed in 2025'), and the systems diagram has one focal hub and one dotted connector grammar; the developer tiles mix per-day, per-second and per-minute rates.

score.reason: T-STAT-TILE passes on the commerce tiles and T-DIAGRAM-FOCAL and T-CONNECTORS pass on the systems diagram; T-STAT-TILE fails on the developer row's mixed periods (DVZ-013) and the diagram runs past the web-card node budget (DVZ-014).

findings.where: 'Scale with confidence.' row, h4.developers-scale-subsection__stats-grid-item-heading (three tiles), 1440, contact sheet #4, #6, #7, tiles/1440-11.png
findings.evidence: The three figures in one row use three periods: '500m+ API requests per day', '10k+ API requests per second' and '150k+ transactions per minute'. 500 million a day is about 5,800 a second, so the reader has to do arithmetic to see that the 10k figure is a peak rather than an average, and the tile does not say so.
findings.before: Three rates on three time bases in one row.
findings.after: Put all three on one time base and name peak or average, for example '10k+ API requests per second at peak', '5,800 per second on average' and the transaction rate per second.
findings.why: Tiles in a row invite comparison; different time bases make the comparison wrong unless the reader converts them.

findings.where: 'Connect to existing systems.' diagram, svg.developer-systems-animation__center-path-svg (aria-hidden), 1440, contact sheet #1 and #2, tiles/1440-10.png
findings.evidence: The diagram holds about twenty nodes: five systems (ERP, CRM, Subscriptions, Legacy billing, Booking system), five methods (SDK, Event Destinations, App Marketplace, Data Pipeline, Orchestration), the Stripe hub, a four-logo partner block with two empty slots, a Snowflake logo and four boxes all labelled 'PSP'. The partner and warehouse logos carry no names.
findings.before: A twenty-node board in a web card, with unnamed logos.
findings.after: Keep the hub and the five methods as the diagram, name each logo, and move the system list into the caption or a row of text above it.
findings.why: Conflict C54 puts a web card's budget at about 12 nodes; past it, the five integration methods (the point of the section) share the eye with logos the reader has to recognise.

strengths: The commerce tiles state qualifier and period in words under each figure: '135+ currencies and payment methods supported', 'US$1.9tn in payments volume processed in 2025', '99.999% historical uptime for Stripe services', '200m+ active subscriptions managed on Stripe Billing'.

The systems diagram has one focal node (the Stripe hub), one connector style (thin dotted orthogonal lines) and labelled method boxes on every path; the svg carries a full text description of the diagram.
The terminal mock shows a single amount ('€26.89') as a payment screen, not as a chart.
